001package com.streamConverter.path;
002
003import java.util.ArrayList;
004import java.util.Arrays;
005import java.util.List;
006import java.util.Objects;
007import java.util.stream.Collectors;
008
009/**
010 * Simplified tree path class for hierarchical path matching.
011 *
012 * <p>This class provides simple path matching against List&lt;String&gt; hierarchical paths. It
013 * supports both JSON-style ("$.user.name") and XML-style ("user/name") path formats.
014 */
015public class TreePath extends AbstractPath<List<String>> {
016
017  // Internal hierarchical representation as simple string list
018  private final List<String> pathSegments;
019  private final String originalPath;
020
021  // === Constructors ===
022
023  /**
024   * Creates TreePath from path string (auto-detects JSON or XML format)
025   *
026   * @param pathExpression Path expression (e.g., "$.user.name" or "user/name")
027   */
028  public TreePath(String pathExpression) {
029    super(pathExpression);
030    this.originalPath = pathExpression;
031    this.pathSegments = parsePathToSegments(pathExpression);
032  }
033
034  /**
035   * Creates TreePath from JSON format path
036   *
037   * @param jsonPath JSON format path (e.g., "$.user.name", "$.items.title")
038   * @return TreePath instance
039   */
040  public static TreePath fromJsonPath(String jsonPath) {
041    return new TreePath(jsonPath);
042  }
043
044  /**
045   * Creates TreePath from XML format path
046   *
047   * @param xmlPath XML format path (e.g., "user/name", "items/title")
048   * @return TreePath instance
049   */
050  public static TreePath fromXmlPath(String xmlPath) {
051    return new TreePath(xmlPath);
052  }
053
054  // === AbstractPath Implementation ===
055
056  @Override
057  protected void validateAndNormalize(String rawPath) {
058    if (rawPath == null || rawPath.trim().isEmpty()) {
059      throw new IllegalArgumentException("TreePath cannot be null or empty");
060    }
061  }
062
063  @Override
064  public boolean matches(List<String> currentPath) {
065    if (currentPath == null) {
066      return false;
067    }
068
069    // Simple exact match comparison
070    return pathSegments.equals(currentPath);
071  }
072
073  // === Internal Implementation ===
074
075  private List<String> parsePathToSegments(String pathExpression) {
076    String trimmed = pathExpression.trim();
077
078    // Handle JSON format (starts with "$.")
079    if (trimmed.startsWith("$.")) {
080      String pathWithoutRoot = trimmed.substring(2);
081      if (pathWithoutRoot.isEmpty()) {
082        return new ArrayList<>();
083      }
084      return Arrays.asList(pathWithoutRoot.split("\\."));
085    }
086
087    // Handle XML format (simple path separated by "/")
088    if (trimmed.contains("/")) {
089      String normalizedPath = trimmed.replaceAll("^/+", "").replaceAll("/+$", "");
090      if (normalizedPath.isEmpty()) {
091        return new ArrayList<>();
092      }
093      // Split and filter out empty segments caused by multiple consecutive slashes
094      return Arrays.stream(normalizedPath.split("/"))
095          .filter(segment -> !segment.isEmpty())
096          .collect(Collectors.toList());
097    }
098
099    // Single segment
100    return List.of(trimmed);
101  }
102
103  @Override
104  public String toString() {
105    return originalPath;
106  }
107
108  @Override
109  public boolean equals(Object obj) {
110    if (this == obj) return true;
111    if (obj == null || getClass() != obj.getClass()) return false;
112    TreePath treePath = (TreePath) obj;
113    return Objects.equals(pathSegments, treePath.pathSegments);
114  }
115
116  @Override
117  public int hashCode() {
118    return Objects.hash(pathSegments);
119  }
120}
